verses.text: Here is the family record of Noah's sons—Shem, Ham, and Japheth. They had children after the flood.
Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
Their descendants spread across the islands and coastlands, dividing the lands among them by language, family, and nation.
Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah's sons were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush became the father of Nimrod, who grew into a powerful figure on earth.
He was a mighty hunter in Yahweh's sight. That's why people say, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter in Yahweh's sight."
His kingdom first included Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar.
From there he went into Assyria and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, and Calah,
along with Resen, between Nineveh and the great city of Calah.
Mizraim became the father of the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
the Pathrusim, Casluhim (from whom the Philistines descended), and Caphtorim.
Canaan became the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth,
and of the Jebusites, Amorites, and Girgashites,
Hivites, Arkites, and Sinites,
Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites. Later, the Canaanite families spread out.
The Canaanite territory stretched from Sidon toward Gerar and Gaza, then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These were Ham's descendants, grouped by families, languages, lands, and nations.
Sons were also born to Shem, Japheth's older brother. Shem was the ancestor of all the children of Eber.
Shem's sons were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
Aram's sons were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arpachshad became the father of Shelah, and Shelah became the father of Eber.
Eber had two sons. One was named Peleg, because the earth was divided in his days; his brother was named Joktan.
Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Obal, Abimael, and Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All of these were Joktan's sons.
Their territory stretched from Mesha toward Sephar, the eastern mountain country.
These were Shem's descendants, grouped by families, languages, lands, and nations.
These were the families descended from Noah's sons, listed by generations and nations. After the flood, the nations spread across the earth.
